svg.title: The upgrade test's three phases, and what each gate reads
svg.desc: Phase one installs the previous pinned chart versions from a scratch commit with make up. Phase two publishes the pinned revision and lets Argo CD converge, behind five gates: the publish landed, read from the mirror ref inside the git-server pod and Argo CD's resolved revision rather than local HEAD; the root rewrote the child Application specs; every Application reached Synced and Healthy and held for thirty seconds; targetRevision equals the pinned version, which reads desired state only; and the workloads carry the pinned images, read from running pods rather than the Deployment spec. Phase three rolls back by re-pointing Argo CD rather than by helm rollback, and its outcome is decided by the classification diagram.
svg.text: The upgrade test, and what each gate reads
Three phases against one cluster. Two gates are worded by what they read, because the obvious version of each passed on a real defect.
PHASE 1
Install the previous pins
A scratch commit carrying the previous chart versions, then a full bring-up.
scratch commit
make up
previous pins
PHASE 2 · the upgrade, behind five gates
Publish the pinned revision, let Argo CD converge
Each gate below names what it reads. Converging is not the same as upgrading.
1 the publish landed
reads the mirror ref inside the git-server pod — not local HEAD
2 the root rewrote the child Application specs
reads the four version-pinned children
3 every Application Synced + Healthy, held 30s
reads Argo CD's verdict on its own work
4 targetRevision == pinned
reads DESIRED state only
5 the workloads carry the pinned images
reads RUNNING PODS — not the Deployment spec
Gates 1 and 5 are orange because each replaced a version that passed on a real defect. A spec that moved while no container did satisfies 1 through 4.
PHASE 3
Roll back — an Argo CD re-point, not helm rollback
Republish the older revision as main and let Argo CD converge backward. What a failure here means is decided by the classification diagram.
helm rollback was rejected rather than overlooked: every component is owned by an Application with selfHeal and prune, so it would be reverted within seconds.
